answer: Each identity claims one opal seam shaft and locks a 70-credit bond, registering it publicly. Each epoch it files a pulse log driven by a gale, return timed at the mouth. An auditor recomputes the return from the gale table; over 5 percent off, or a reused pulse serial, burns the bond. First shaft fee 30; the k-th is 30+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,024 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,027,000 plus 70,000 locked, fees follow shaft order. A rented-shaft ring fails: a borrowed pulse keeps its home key and gale time, never matching the claimed shaft. An honest miner pays 30 once and recovers the bond.
